title: AI code review model response (v2 - checklist citations)
description: The only shape the model may return. Enforced by review_agent/parser.py. A response failing this schema triggers exactly one stricter retry; a second failure ends the run as a degraded review (exit 3), never as partial or invented feedback. Change from v1 (feature 001): a checklist violation now cites `item_id` and `document` instead of free-text `item` + `source`, because rules now come from several Excel and Word documents and a filename alone is no longer traceable (FR-027, research R12). A violation whose `item_id` is not present in the combined checklist supplied with the prompt is DROPPED by the parser and counted in the report as a hallucinated citation - it is never posted.

coverage.description: One entry per acceptance criterion of the linked story. Empty array when no work item is linked (FR-024).

criterion.description: The acceptance criterion, quoted or closely paraphrased from the story.

status.description: appears_addressed: the diff plausibly implements it. not_addressed: no related changes - NEUTRAL, never a defect, never a comment, never changes the exit code (Principle V). possible_contradiction: the diff conflicts with it.

evidence.description: What in the diff supports this status. Must reference the diff, not speculate about code not shown.

checklist_violations.description: Only real violations of the combined checklist. An empty array is the correct answer for a clean diff - do not invent stylistic filler (FR-029).

item_id.description: The identifier of the violated checklist item, copied EXACTLY from the combined checklist supplied in the prompt (for example 'SEC-WEB-01' or 'NFR-v2.0:Arch Quality Attributes:17'). An identifier not present in that checklist causes the finding to be dropped.

item_title.description: The title of that checklist item, for readability in the posted comment.

document.description: Filename of the checklist document the item came from, exactly as labelled in the combined checklist (FR-027).

issue.description: How this diff violates that item.

severity.description: Optional. Echo the severity the checklist item carries, where it carries one. Never invent a severity the document does not state.

file.description: Repo-relative path from the diff, or omitted when the violation is not file-specific.

line.description: Line in the post-change file. 0 or omitted means no specific line - the finding then routes to the summary comment instead of an inline comment (FR-036).

code_issues.description: Defects visible in the diff text. Not style preferences, and not anything requiring the code to be run. Reported for the reviewer's information; nothing here gates a merge (Principle VI).

severity.description: high: incorrect behaviour, data loss, or a security problem. medium: a real defect with limited blast radius. low: worth knowing.

file.description: Repo-relative path from the diff, or omitted when not file-specific.

line.description: Line in the post-change file. 0 or omitted routes the finding to the summary comment.

summary.description: Plain-language overall summary for the developer. Reports what the change does and what is worth a human's attention. Never asserts that unaddressed criteria are defects.
